sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief on Togo
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 28 August 2026; reports 2026 crop conditions, June 2026 flooding and the 2026 lean season.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS integrates crop monitoring, food-security classification and market information.
sources.limitations: Snapshot; seasonal outlook is not a final 2026 harvest result.

sources.title: Response in Coastal Countries Linked to Sahel Crisis Spillover: Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2, End of Year 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF regional report covering 1 January to 31 December 2024; published 14 April 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF regional annual situation report with country-level humanitarian needs and programme reporting.
sources.limitations: The Togo chapter is operational and its displacement and access figures describe 2024, not current prevalence.

sources.title: Togo Hydromet and Early Warning Services
sources.temporal_coverage: WMO project portfolio page lists the project as completed; the accessible page does not state dates.
sources.methodology: WMO project portfolio page lists objectives, partners and output areas.
sources.limitations: The page lists outputs but does not report which were delivered or measure resulting forecast or warning performance.

sources.title: Analyse du paysage climatique pour les enfants au Togo: Placer les droits des enfants au cœur de l’action climatique
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Forest Resources of Togo, with support from the United Nations Children’s Fund
sources.temporal_coverage: Publisher webpage summary for the French-language Ministry–UNICEF climate landscape for children, published November 2025.
sources.methodology: Accessible publisher summary identifies the report authors and summarizes child-focused climate risks and policy findings.
sources.limitations: The underlying 19 MB French report was not readable; the page summary gives national themes without local estimates or detailed methods.

claims.locator: Section ‘Generally favourable performance of 2026 seasonal rains’, paragraphs on northern planting and vegetation.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports that early-season dryness and erratic rain delayed planting and required replanting in parts of Kara and Savanes; early-August satellite data showed below-average vegetation pockets in northern Kara.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: Dated crop snapshot, not a final yield or household-loss estimate.

claims.locator: Section ‘About 332 000 people estimated to face severe acute food insecurity between June and August 2026’.
claims.paraphrase: At its 28 August 2026 reference date, FAO placed about 45% of the population estimated to face CH Phase 3 food insecurity in Savanes; attacks, insecurity-driven livelihood and trade disruption, and about 13,400 IDPs were reported there.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: The 45% is of nationally estimated CH3 population; IDPs counted as of June 2026.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO identifies civil insecurity as a key driver of acute food insecurity and says attacks disrupted livelihoods and trade and triggered displacement in Savanes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Section ‘About 332 000 people estimated to face severe acute food insecurity between June and August 2026’, final paragraphs.

claims.locator: Final paragraph on heavy rainfall and flooding.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports late-June 2026 heavy rain flooded Greater Lomé and parts of Maritime and Plateaux, affecting about 26,600 people and damaging housing and infrastructure.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: Aggregate affected population; no locality losses or household outcomes.

claims.locator: Togo ‘Situation Overview & Humanitarian Needs’, paragraph on Savanes security incidents in 2024.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports 16 IED explosions in 2024 limited emergency actors’ access in Kpendjal, Kpendjal Ouest, Tône and Tandjoaré; 31 armed-group attacks or incursions caused 49 deaths and displacement.
claims.limitations: UNICEF's annual operational report does not identify which individual response activities were blocked.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF says 16 IED explosions restricted emergency-actor access and armed-group attacks caused deaths and displacement in named Savanes prefectures.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Togo ‘Situation Overview & Humanitarian Needs’, paragraph on Savanes security incidents in 2024.

claims.locator: Togo ‘Situation Overview & Humanitarian Needs’, paragraph on the 2024 rainy season.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports a bad 2024 rainy season flooded Maritime and Grand Lomé, affecting 42,000 people; its regional overview says floods damaged crops and infrastructure and displaced communities.
claims.limitations: The report gives a combined regional affected count, not flood losses by locality.

claims.locator: Togo ‘Situation Overview & Humanitarian Needs’, paragraphs on displacement and service access.
claims.paraphrase: By October 2024, UNICEF recorded 49,607 displaced people nationally, including 39,436 refugees and 10,171 IDPs; it reports displaced people in 71 Savanes localities had limited access to water, sanitation, health care, education and protection services.
claims.limitations: These are October 2024 figures; service constraints are not quantified by locality.

claims.locator: Project background, objectives and Components A–B under ‘Outputs’.
claims.paraphrase: WMO lists its completed Togo project as supporting meteorological, hydrological and civil-protection capacity, climate-watch forecasting, pilot flood and food-security warnings, multi-hazard procedures and community contingency exercises.
geographies: communities in flood- and agricultural-drought-prone areas
claims.limitations: The completed project page lists output areas but does not verify delivery or warning effectiveness.

claims.paraphrase: The Ministry–UNICEF climate-landscape summary says prolonged drought, recurring floods, coastal erosion and rising temperatures threaten children’s rights and access to safe water, food, education, health care and protection.
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Forest Resources of Togo
claims.limitations: This is a national webpage summary; it provides no local exposure estimates or detailed report methods.

claims.paraphrase: The summary cites Togo’s 2025 climate-change law as governance progress but says children’s and young people’s needs remain insufficiently integrated into public policy; it recommends resilient essential services and youth participation.
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Forest Resources of Togo
claims.limitations: The recommendations describe the report's policy agenda, not completed implementation or measured results.

search_audit.query: Togo 2024 2025 floods climate impacts Savanes Kara Oti Plateaux official report FAO UNICEF
search_audit.outcome: Found FAO's 2026 named-region crop and flood update and UNICEF's 2024 report on floods in Maritime/Grand Lomé and displacement and service-access conditions in Savanes.

search_audit.query: Togo climate drought farmer herder conflict Savanes climate security conflict pathway primary report 2024 2025
search_audit.outcome: FAO says civil insecurity drives acute food insecurity and disrupts livelihoods/trade in Savanes; UNICEF reports attacks, displacement and access constraints. Neither inspected source attributes the violence to climate hazards; no link is inferred.

search_audit.query: Togo Savanes insecurity violence disrupted climate adaptation flood resilience agriculture access 2024 2025 report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF reports that 2024 IED explosions in named Savanes prefectures restricted emergency-actor access; FAO reports ongoing insecurity-related livelihood and trade disruption. No inspected source evaluates armed violence blocking a specific climate-adaptation project.

search_audit.query: Togo local climate resilience adaptation community project flood drought outcomes 2024 2025 government UN World Bank
search_audit.outcome: Found WMO's completed hydromet/early-warning project page listing forecast, flood-warning and community contingency output areas; it does not verify results. The UNICEF child climate-landscape webpage summarizes national policy and service-resilience findings; its 19 MB report PDF was inaccessible.

gaps: No inspected new source establishes that climate hazards caused armed-group violence, farmer-herder conflict or other violence in Togo; the new evidence reports insecurity-related food and access effects without inferring climate causation.
The UNICEF 2024 report's attacks and access restrictions refer to 2024; they are not evidence of current access conditions in October 2026.
FAO's 28 August 2026 crop brief is a dated snapshot; seasonal projections were not presented as verified harvest outcomes.
WMO lists the hydromet project as completed but does not document delivered outputs or warning effectiveness on the accessible page.
The full French UNICEF Climate Landscape report exceeded the reader's 19 MB limit; only the publisher summary page was reviewed, so claims lack local disaggregation and detailed methods.
The IFRC 2025 mid-year download was rejected as application/octet-stream and GCF SAP048 returned 403; no findings from their search excerpts were used.
